title: PRD: Hosted endpoints - service-level profiles (quality lanes) + launch readiness
creator: Maya Rodriguez
description: This PRD defines a set of explicit service-level profiles ("quality lanes") for Redwood hosted inference endpoints (chat, completions, embeddings, rerank). Quality lanes are prescriptive configuration bundles that map developer intent (e.g., low-latency, high-quality, cost-sensitive) to runtime configuration, model variant selection, and SLA guarantees. The goal is to give product teams clear, documented contracts for behavior and economics while enabling safe rollouts and operational observability.
background: Customers frequently ask for a simple knob to pick latency vs cost vs quality guarantees. Current hosted endpoints expose knobs (model, max_tokens, temperature, batching) but lack a first-class, documented profile that maps to SLOs and fallback behavior. This increases onboarding time, increases incorrect config usage, and makes rollouts harder for Dedicated/Private parity.
goals: Provide 3 canonical quality lanes: low-latency, balanced, high-quality
Define precise behavioral contracts for each lane across chat/completions/embeddings/rerank
Publish acceptance tests and telemetry thresholds for launch
Ship SDK flags and Console UI to select lanes
Ensure compatibility with Dedicated and Private runtimes
non_goals: Introduce new model training or model weights
Replace per-request model override; lanes should be advisory but enforceable by tiers only where required
Full automatic conversion of historical configs
scope_changes: During scoping we removed an initial plan to include multi-turn stateful-slot management in lane guarantees; that will be a follow-up. We also narrowed the initial embeddings lane to not enforce quantization profiles in Private until KMS audit is complete.
requirements: API: Add optional 'service_lane' parameter to inference requests (values: 'latency', 'balanced', 'quality')
Runtime: Map lane to model variants and kernel/quantization profiles via compilation table
SLO: Define 99th percentile latency and token cost targets for each lane per model class
Console: Dropdown to set default account lane and per-endpoint override
SDK: Expose lane in SDK request options and ensure streaming is unaffected
Telemetry: Emit lane tag on all traces, logs and cost attributions
Rollout: Canary to 1% then 10% before global flip with automatic rollback on SLA breaches
Docs: PRD-style doc + migration guide for customers currently pinning models
acceptance_criteria: Endpoint accepts service_lane and returns it in response metadata
Runtime honors lane mapping for at least two model families (causal-xx and chat-yy)
SLOs validated in staging: latency lane meets 99th percentile latency target with at least 95% traffic in staging
Billing shows per-lane cost attribution in Console for sample workload
E2E tests for chat/completions/embeddings/rerank pass with lane flag set
Canary automation triggers rollback when SLA breach defined in 'failure_conditions' is met
Docs and SDKs published in docs.redwood.ai and npm/pypi packages updated
failure_conditions: >=2.0x baseline 99p latency regression sustained for 30 minutes
Error rate increase in production >0.5% absolute and >200 errors/min
Token cost deviation >25% above expected estimate for balanced lane across 1 hour
launch_checklist: API spec merged and versioned (OpenAPI + SDKs)
Runtime compile table entries for lane->model mappings merged
Staging telemetry dashboards for lane-level SLOs created
Canary automation (1%, 10%, 100%) configured with health checks
Console UI: default account lane dropdown and endpoint override merged behind flag
Docs: PRD, acceptance tests, migration guide published
Support playbook with rollback runbook and customer communication templates prepared
Security review signed-off and KMS gating for Private confirmed
Beta program: identify 5 pilot customers (internal + 4 external) and run 2-week validation
rollout_plan: Start with a closed beta for existing enterprise accounts that use Dedicated. Run a 2-week validation focusing on latency and cost telemetry. If stable, enable canary on hosted for 1% traffic for 48 hours, then 10% for 24 hours, then full rollout. Automated rollback conditions tied to lane SLOs. Coordinate customer comms and opt-out windows.
monitoring_and_alerting: Lane-tagged traces and spans in distributed tracing
Per-lane 95/99 latency dashboards by model family
Per-lane token cost burn rate and anomalies
Alerts: sustained 99p latency regression, elevated error rate, cost anomaly per lane
testing_plan: Unit tests for API parsing and response metadata
Integration tests mapping lane->model in runtime harness
Load tests simulating mixed-lane traffic at 2x expected peak
Behavioral tests: prompt suites verifying answer stability across lanes
Evals: quality regressions measured for 'quality' lane vs balanced baseline
migration_notes: Existing customers who rely on explicit model pins will continue to be supported; service_lane is optional. Migration guide includes recommended mappings from common model pins to lanes, examples for SDK usage, and guidance for Dedicated/Private customers who want to pin lanes at cluster or pool level.
open_questions: Should lanes be enforced or advisory for self-serve hosted tiers? Recommendation: advisory for free/standard, enforceable for enterprise with SLA contracts
Do we require model-family parity for all lanes at launch? Recommendation: support two families and document gaps
How to present lane cost estimates in Console without confusing pricing? Need design mock and legal review
